selection_rule: Best of initial three; replace on two paired wins and mean gain >= 0.002

ensemble.rule: Best per visited route; max 3 routes; equal probability weights; inner gain >= .002

confirmation.selection_rule: Best of initial three; replace on two paired wins and mean gain >= 0.002

proposal.reason: Trial 1 used word-only features with C=0.3 and achieved high accuracy but near-zero spam recall, so macro_f1 was dominated by the ham class. Selecting word+char features with C=3.0 broadens the representation and reduces regularization strength, directly targeting the observed minority-class failure while staying within the available shared baselines.
proposal.review: The only completed primary trial is single_word_C0.3 with macro_f1 0.5081 and class recalls [1.0, 0.0404]. This indicates the current model is not identifying spam on the search split; the next trial should test a representation and regularization change rather than replicate the same configuration.
proposal.hypothesis: Word+char n-gram features with C=3.0 may capture spam-indicative substrings and reduce underfitting relative to word-only C=0.3, potentially improving spam recall and macro_f1. This is a diagnostic improvement attempt, not a guaranteed gain.
proposal.uncertainty: Direction and magnitude are uncertain. The primary split is small, and trial 1's low spam recall may persist; stronger fitting could also overfit or trade off ham recall, so the effect on macro_f1 is not known in advance.
